label: input d/i (also r,f,a,0) after k/u/n/e/q/v/2 seen earlier
explanation: Mainly a token-identity unit: it fires when the current input is d (rate 9%, 33% of activation mass) or i (6%, 21%), and less often for r, f, a or 0. It fires in both the original and copy phases, never at t=0 or at the delimiter step. Whether it fires depends on context: it is much more likely when tokens from {k,u,n,e,q,v,2} came earlier in the sequence (e.g. prev2_tok k gives 3.9x lift; output target u or k in the copy phase gives 3-6x), and it is also elevated at the first copy step (recall_idx 1). The predicate captures 66% of active steps and 76% of activation mass on dev, but precision is only about 10%: most d/i inputs with that context still do not fire, so the gating is not fully described. The strongest activations are on d (or the first re-input token) late in the original phase or at the first copy step, in sequences rich in k/u/n. Activation is weak on inputs outside the d/i/r/f/a/0 set and on repeated tokens (in_count >= 3).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=d (+6.75), in_tok=i (+6.23), t=1 & prev_tok=k (+6.02), in_tok=r (+5.21), in_tok=a (+4.98), in_tok=0 (+4.75). Lower it: prev2_tok=- (-4.53), phase=1 & in_tok=<DEL> (-3.40), in_tok=k (-2.56), orig4=- (-2.51).
